title: 72hr-escalator-cadence: contingency matrix & condensed release notes template
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures a compact release cadence we're experimenting with (72hr Escalator), plus a small contingency matrix and a pared-down release-notes template for external/internal distribution. Aim: enable rapid launches with clear ramp/fallout actions while minimizing cognitive load for operators. This is intentionally condensed for fast handoffs.

Scope / When to use:
- Small-to-medium infra and runtime changes (non-breaking API, config flips, model rollout variants)
- When stakeholder SLAs accept a 72hr watch window rather than multi-week phased rollouts
- NOT for major DB migrations, schema changes, or regulatory blocks

High-level 72hr Escalator timeline (owner in parens):
- T-72 to T-24: Preflight & dry-run (Release Lead: Anika)
  - Smoke test bundle (automated + manual subset)
  - Canary in single AZ with synthetic traffic profile
  - Telemetry sampling toggled to 100% for affected routes
  - Stakeholder sync + comm pre-announce

- T-24 to T-0: Gradual ramp and traffic shaping (Traffic Lead: Luis)
  - 10% -> 30% -> 60% incremental ramps at 6-hour marks if SLOs stable
  - KV cache priming and warmup tasks executed at 30% step
  - Predefined abort checkpoints at each step (see triggers)

- T0 to T+24: Full production lift & observation (Ops Lead: Maya)
  - Autoscaler profiles locked for 6 hours post T0 to avoid oscillation
  - Telemetry stitching to build end-to-end traces for new paths
  - Begin condensed post-deploy notes (template below)

- T+24 to T+72: Watch + rollback window (SRE: Samir)
  - Canary artifacts retained and archived at T+72 for debug
  - If no regression and business metrics stable, mark as staged->general availability at T+72
  - After T+72, consider removal of elevated telemetry if cost-limited

Preflight checklist (quick, binary checks) - T-72
- [ ] Release branch created and PRs merged, builds green (CI jobs: unit+integration)
- [ ] Canary config prepared and smoke test slug exists
- [ ] Rollback artifact available and smoke-tested (exact commit/tag)
- [ ] Capacity checklist: GPUs reserved / cluster headroom >= 20%
- [ ] Observability: dashboards for latency, errors, token-throughput, p95/p99 defined and pinned
- [ ] Alert contact roster loaded and pager schedule verified
- [ ] Legal/Compliance signoff present (if applicable)

Contingency matrix (quick lookup)
- Symptom: Token latency p95 jumps > 2x baseline for >10 minutes
  - Immediate: Pause ramp, move traffic back to previous variant (Traffic Lead)
  - If persists after rollback: Open incident, engage SRE on-call, escalate to Release Lead
  - Notes: capture sample request ids and stack traces; save KV cache snapshot

- Symptom: Error rate (5xx) increases >1% absolute and sustained 5+ minutes
  - Immediate: Stop rollout (Traffic Lead), start traffic draining of new variant
  - Remediation: redeploy previous stable image, run targeted integration tests
  - Postmortem: collect histogram of error codes and compaction of traces

- Symptom: Downstream dependency (DB, auth, external model store) misbehaves
  - Immediate: Switch to fallback path (if available), enable degraded mode flag
  - If no fallback: Rollback and open P1 ticket with dependency owner

- Symptom: Cost spike (token generation cost up >30% expected)
  - Immediate: Engage Product & Finance, throttle non-essential routes, enable cheaper model variant routing
  - Longer term: schedule Optimize assessment (quantization/batching tweaks)

Communication playbook (short strokes)
- Pre-announce (T-48): Slack #release-ops summary + stakeholder email (pm, support, legal)
- Live updates: standup every 4 hours during T-24 -> T+24 window in #release-ops; release lead posts concise status messages (OK / BRIEF ISSUE / ROLLING BACK)
- Escalation: use paging policy for P1s + zoom bridge (auto-join link in JIRA ticket)
- Postmortem: one-week timeline; initial blameless triage within 48 hours

Condensed release notes template (for client-facing and internal variants):
- Title: <short descriptor> (internal tag: release-YYYYMMDD-xx)
- TL;DR (1 sentence): what changed and why
- User-visible impact (bullets): new behavior, performance changes, any opt-in flags
- Ops notes (short): rollout cadence used, canaries/percentages, rollback commit/tag
- Known limitations / TODOs: brief list
- Rollback instructions (one-liners): quick commands or Jira link to rollback play
- Contact: pager + on-call + runbook link

Example (filled):
- Title: latency-fix-encoder-opt-20270915 (internal: release-20270915-01)
- TL;DR: Improve model encoder batching to reduce p95 latency by ~20% for short prompts
- User-visible impact: better latency on text-gen API; no API changes
- Ops notes: 72hr escalator used; canaries at 10/30/60%; rollback tag: v20270915-rollback-a1
- Known limitations: slight throughput regression at sequence length >4096 in older GPUs
- Rollback: run `ops rollback release v20270915-rollback-a1` (see playbook)
- Contact: pager@redwood.team, release runbook: Confluence:RELEASE-RUN-72HR-2027

Open questions / TODOs (working list)
- Do we want a hard requirement for a second reviewer on all 72hr cadences? (pros: safety; cons: slower) -- @Luis to propose a quick SLAB
- Can we short-circuit T-24->T0 ramps for low-risk infra flips? Need a small risk rubric
- Automation: Add a canned Slack message generator that populates percent steps and rollback commands

Notes to self / rough ops snippets
- Quick rollback CLI: `ops release rollback --tag vYYYYMMDD --force-checks` (needs SSO token)
- Cheap fallback route: route-model=redwood-small-quantized (adds 2-3% error-likelihood for hallucination)
- Sampling query ids: `trace.sample --route <route> --since T-1h --limit 200`

References / links
- Confluence:RELEASE-RUN-72HR-2027 (detailed playbook)
- JIRA:RELEASE-2027-092 (this release ticket)
- GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-scripts/pull/412 (ramp automation)

If this model works for the next two pilots, I'll convert the condensed release notes template into a small script that autopopulates the TL;DR fields and stamps rollback tags. Feedback welcome — particularly on the abort thresholds and whether 10/30/60 is the right progression for our traffic mix.

-- Anika (release lead)
summary: Draft of a compact 72-hour release cadence with preflight checklist, contingency matrix for common failure modes, condensed release notes template for rapid distribution, communication playbook, and open action items for automation and policy decisions.
